---
title: "The workspace in the IDE"
subtitle: "Foundation – six steps in the workspace of the case"
---

The IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), short for integrated development environment, is the program from which you drive R. It holds your files, runs your code and shows you what the code produced. The umbrella site of the course teaches it in [Positron and other IDEs](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html), a module that treats Positron in detail, with briefer sections on RStudio, VS Code, other editors and the browser lab, and that sets its tasks in the workspace of the housing-audit case. This page holds the part that belongs to the EU-frames case: six steps through the workspace of this case, the folder that you download and open in your IDE. The download and install steps for each IDE on Windows, macOS and Linux are on the [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html), and the problems that come up are on the [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html).

The workspace of this case switches the AI features of Positron and VS Code off for its whole folder, for the reason set out in the [section on licensed data](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ai.html#sec-licensed) of the module on AI assistants.

## The six steps {#sec-try}

Work through these six steps in the workspace of the EU-frames case, in whichever IDE you chose. Together they use every pane that the exercise needs. Download the zip of the workspace from the [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace) and unzip it first; the folder that it holds is called `replication-lab-main`.

1. Open the workspace folder: File → Open Folder in Positron and VS Code, or `replication-lab.Rproj` inside it in RStudio. The files appear in the side bar: the report `index.qmd`, the script `working_script.R`, and the folders `R/`, `data/` and `prep/`.
2. Open `R/check_setup.R` and run it as a whole, with the button at the top of the editor that runs or sources the file, or with `source("R/check_setup.R")` in the console. Read the OK and FAIL lines in the console; the check script of this workspace has no reference fit to report.
3. Run `euframes <- readr::read_csv("data/EUframes_cy.csv")` in the console, then open the data frame in the data viewer: from the Variables pane or with `View(euframes)`. In Positron, read the summary panel: how many rows, which columns have missing values and how many, and how the rows are spread across the countries and the years. You should find 270 rows, 27 countries in each of ten years.
4. Filter the view to one country and sort by year, then confirm that the object in the session is unchanged by running `nrow(euframes)` in the console.
5. Draw one figure, `tinyplot::tinyplot(mcosmo ~ unemp, data = euframes)`, the framing score against the unemployment rate, and find it in the plots pane; export it once, so that you know where the button is.
6. Open `index.qmd`, the report of the exercise, and render it, with Preview in Positron and VS Code or Render in RStudio. Find the finished document in the viewer, and the file that the render wrote, `index.html`, in the `_site` folder.

If any of the six fails, the [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) has the likely causes, and the [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) the steps to repeat.
